requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: A structured type MAY be subtyped as given in table 3.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows subtyping of structured types as given in table 3.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype
requirements.canonical: A value of a subtype SHALL fulfil the constraint of the subtype and all constraints of all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.
requirements.original: Values of a subtype shall fulfil conditions specified by its constraint and all constraints existing in all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: The number of elements of a value of a record of or set of type MAY be constrained.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits constraining the number of elements in instances of record of and set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS written as the `length` keyword followed by a single value or a range with inclusive boundaries in parentheses, placed between the `record` or `set` keyword and the `of` keyword.
requirements.original: The length keyword followed by a value or a range (with inclusive boundaries only) within brackets and used between the record or set and the of keywords, restricts the allowed number of elements for the given record of or set of type.

ambiguity.issue: 'brackets' is used for the parentheses enclosing the length value or range.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS restricting the allowed number of elements of values of that type to the given value or range.
requirements.original: The length keyword followed by a value or a range (with inclusive boundaries only) within brackets and used between the record or set and the of keywords, restricts the allowed number of elements for the given record of or set of type.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The value or the bounds of a length restriction of a record of or set of type SHALL be non-negative integer values, except for an upper bound given as `infinity`.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `infinity` keyword MAY be used as the upper bound of a length restriction range of a record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: If `infinity` is used as the upper bound of a length restriction, the maximum number of elements IS NOT constrained.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The upper bound of a length restriction range SHALL NOT be less than the lower bound.
requirements.original: In case of the range syntax the upper bound shall not be lesser than the lower bound value.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of or set of type definition MAY be used as parent type to define a new record of or set of subtype.
requirements.original: Record of and set of type definitions may be used to define new record of or set of subtypes.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: When a new record of or set of subtype is defined from a referenced record of or set of type, the `length` keyword and the value or range SHALL be placed following the identifier of the new type.
requirements.original: In this case the rules of the previous paragraph apply, except that the length keyword and the value or range defining the allowed number of iterations (within brackets) shall be placed following the identifier of the new type.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The rules on the value and bounds of a length restriction (non-negative integers, `infinity` upper bound, upper bound not less than lower bound) SHALL also apply to length subtyping of referenced record of and set of types.
requirements.original: In this case the rules of the previous paragraph apply, except that the length keyword and the value or range defining the allowed number of iterations (within brackets) shall be placed following the identifier of the new type.

requirements.subject: ent:constant
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression of length subtyping SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of length subtyping shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: List subtyping MAY be used when defining a new type based on an existing parent type.
requirements.original: List subtyping is possible when defining a new type based on an existing parent type, but not directly at the declaration of the core type (see table 3).

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: List subtyping SHALL NOT be applied directly at the declaration of a core type.
requirements.original: List subtyping is possible when defining a new type based on an existing parent type, but not directly at the declaration of the core type (see table 3).

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: A subtype defined by list subtyping IS restricting its allowed values to the values matched by at least one of the constraints in the list.
requirements.original: Subtypes defined by a list subtyping restrict the allowed values of the subtype to the values matched by at least one of the constraints in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: In list subtyping of record, set, record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and of arrays, the list MAY contain both subtypes and possibly partial templates of the core type.
requirements.original: In case of list subtyping of `record`, `set`, `record of`, `set of`, `union`, `map` and `anytype` types, and arrays, the list may contain both subtypes and possibly partial templates of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: Subtype references in a subtyping list SHALL be resolved recursively, so that the templates denoted by the referenced subtypes become members of an expanded list containing only possibly partial templates.
requirements.original: Subtype references shall be resolved in a recursive way: the collection of templates denoted by the subtype(s) referenced in the list become members of the new subtype definition with an expanded list containing only possibly partial templates.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: Every value present in the expanded list of a list subtype SHALL be a valid value of the parent type.
requirements.original: All values present in the expanded list shall be valid values of the parent type.

requirements.subject: ent:partial-template
requirements.canonical: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
requirements.original: For partial (i.e. incomplete) values, all following rules on templates apply.

ambiguity.issue: 'all following rules on templates' can refer to the rules stated next in this clause or to the general template rules of clause 15; the first reading is chosen because of the word 'following'.
readings: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, all rules on templates of the core language (clause 15) SHALL apply.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record of`, `set of`, `union`, `map` and `anytype` types, and arrays, all templates of the expanded list (i.e. after resolving the subtype references) shall be valid (i.e. complete) values and templates of the core type.

ambiguity.issue: 'valid (i.e. complete) values and templates' leaves open whether matching mechanisms are allowed or only specific values; the reading allowing complete templates is chosen.
readings: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every element of the expanded list SHALL be a complete specific value of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using value list notation SHALL be a complete template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record` and `set` types, templates of the expanded list defined using the value list notation shall be valid (i.e. complete) templates of the core type, while templates of the expanded list defined using the field assignment notation may be partial (i.e. incomplete) templates of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using assignment notation MAY be a partial template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record` and `set` types, templates of the expanded list defined using the value list notation shall be valid (i.e. complete) templates of the core type, while templates of the expanded list defined using the field assignment notation may be partial (i.e. incomplete) templates of the core type.

ambiguity.issue: 'field assignment notation' is used instead of the glossary term 'assignment notation'.

requirements.subject: ent:partial-template
requirements.canonical: In a partial template defined with assignment notation in the expanded list of a record or set list subtype, a field that is not explicitly present SHALL be considered as containing AnyValue if it is mandatory and AnyValueOrNone if it is optional.
requirements.original: In the latter case, the fields that are not explicitly present shall be considered as containing AnyValue for mandatory fields and _AnyValueOrNone_ for optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-user
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 user SHOULD assign new values to single fields of values or templates of list-subtyped record or set types cautiously.
requirements.original: > NOTE: Users should assign new values to single fields of values/templates based on types using list subtyping cautiously: it may happen that the new field value would be valid with other combination(s) of the rest of the fields but causes an erroneous record/set value, when combining with the actual values of the other fields.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: Assigning a new value to a single field of a value of a list-subtyped record or set type CAN cause an erroneous value when the new field value is not allowed in combination with the actual values of the other fields.
requirements.original: > NOTE: Users should assign new values to single fields of values/templates based on types using list subtyping cautiously: it may happen that the new field value would be valid with other combination(s) of the rest of the fields but causes an erroneous record/set value, when combining with the actual values of the other fields.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: A list subtype of an enumerated type SHALL contain only values of the parent type.
requirements.original: In case of `enumerated` types, the template list subtyping shall contain only values of the parent type.

ambiguity.issue: 'template list subtyping' is used instead of 'list subtyping'.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.canonical: A type restriction following the identifier of a newly defined record of or set of type (defined with the `record of` or `set of` keywords) SHALL constrain the innermost type.
requirements.original: A type restriction following the identifier of a newly defined record of or set of type (i.e. when the keywords record and of or set and of are used in the definition) shall constrain the innermost type.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.canonical: The iterated type of a newly defined record of or set of type with a type restriction SHALL be a subset of the innermost type.
requirements.original: The newly defined iterated type shall be a subset of the innermost type.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.condition: the innermost type is a basic type
requirements.canonical: If the innermost type of a record of or set of type is a basic type, the subtyping rules of clause 6.1.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
requirements.original: If the innermost type is a basic type, the subtyping rules in clause 6.1.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.condition: the innermost type references a structured type or anytype
requirements.canonical: If the innermost type of a record of or set of type references a structured type or anytype, the rules of clauses 6.2.13.1 and 6.2.13.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
requirements.original: If the innermost type is referencing a structured type or anytype, the rules in clauses 6.2.13.1 and 6.2.13.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:subtyping-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A subtype definition of a structured type or anytype SHALL NOT mix different subtyping mechanisms (e.g. list and length subtyping).
requirements.original: In the case of structured types and the special type anytype, it is forbidden to mix different subtyping mechanisms (e.g. list and length) in the same definition.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-type
requirements.canonical: Constants, variables and formal parameters of timer type MAY be defined.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to define timer constants, variables and parameters.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters' is used where formal parameters are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-reference
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter of timer type CAN contain a reference to an existing timer or the special value `null`.
requirements.original: These constants, variables or parameters can contain a reference to an existing timer or a special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` of timer type IS an unspecified timer reference.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified timer reference, i.e. can be used for variables to explicitly reference no timer.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be assigned to a timer variable to explicitly reference no timer.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified timer reference, i.e. can be used for variables to explicitly reference no timer.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-reference
requirements.canonical: A timer reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance where the timer is defined.
requirements.original: Timer references have meaning only within the test component instances where the timer is defined, i.e. a timer reference assigned to a timer variable in a test component instance "a1" of type "A" has no meaning in a test component instance "a2" of type "A".

ambiguity.issue: The consequence of using a timer reference in another test component instance (error, or unspecified behaviour) is not stated.
readings: Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined causes a dynamic error.
Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined has unspecified behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-type
requirements.canonical: A value of timer type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: The values of timer type are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

non_requirement.reason: pointer to example 1 of this clause
